notesStmt.note: Whitman composed "Death's Valley" at the request of Harper's editor H. M. Alden, recording receipt of payment for it on 1 September 1889 (see notes to loc.04087). Although Whitman wanted to include "Death's Valley" in Good-Bye My Fancy (1891), he demurred because it had not yet appeared in the magazine and "for the present, the poem is theirs, not ours" (With Walt Whitman in Camden [Oregon House, California: W L Bentley, 1996] 8:110). The current manuscript almost certainly dates to late August 1889.

note.p: This manuscript is a group of lines drafted for the poem "Death's Valley," written for Harper's New Monthly Magazine to accompany a painting by George Inness entitled "The Valley of the Shadow of Death." The magazine delayed using it until after Whitman's death, however; it first appeared in the magazine's April 1892 issue.

lg.l:
Aye, well I know 'tis ghastly to descend
that f valley;
Preachers, musicians, poets, painters, always render it,

Philosophs exploit—the battle⹀field, the ship at
sea, the myriad beds, all lands,

All, all the past have enter'd, the ancientest
humanity we know,

Till now for us under our very eyes spreading
the same to⹀day,
Grim, ready, ‸for our eyes, for entrance, yours and mine, ‸our eyes,
